QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_39

question.text: A 1,000-tree plantation reports carbon sequestration of 20 tCO2e/year. The SIA should:

answer.text: Accept the number at face value

Verify (i) tree species and age-class appropriate sequestration factor, (ii) actual surviving trees physically inspected, (iii) risk of reversal (fire, felling) and 'permanence' disclosure, (iv) double-counting check with any CSR or carbon-credit claim on the same trees

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SAS-500 carbon assessment requires species-specific sequestration factors (e.g., Neem, Teak), age-class, survival inspection, permanence risk, and double-counting check against CSR reports and VCS / Gold-Standard credits sold on the same trees. All four elements must be audited. **The Trap:** Options A, B, D are either uncritical or arbitrary. **Cross-Exam Context:** Carbon double-counting is a live issue also in XV Research Analyst (carbon-credit issuer valuations) and III-A Compliance (BRSR). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Ask the SE upfront: 'Have you sold or pledged carbon credits on this plantation?' If yes, you MUST net those out to avoid double counting in the Social Impact Assessment Report.
